sanskrit: ā ghā tā gacchān uttarā yugāni yatra jāmayaḥ kṛṇavann ajāmi | upa barbṛhi vṛṣabhāya bāhum anyam icchasva subhage patiṃ mat ||
english: May those future ages come where kinswomen make what is not kin. Stretch out your arm to the bull; seek another husband than me, O fortunate one.

sanskrit: kiṃ bhrātāsad yad anāthaṃ bhavāti kim u svasā yan nirṛtir nigacchāt | kāmamūtā bahv etad rapāmi tanvā me tanvaṃ saṃ pipṛgdhi ||
english: What sort of brother is it when one becomes without a protector? What sort of sister when dissolution overtakes her? Moved by desire, I speak much of this—mingle your body with my body.

sanskrit: na vā u te tanvā tanvaṃ saṃ papṛcyāṃ pāpam āhur yaḥ svasāraṃ nigacchāt | anyena mat taḥ pramudaḥ kalpayasva na te bhrātā subhage vaṣṭy etat ||
english: Indeed I would not mingle my body with your body—they call it sin when one goes to his sister. Seek your delight with another than me; your brother does not desire this, O fortunate one.

sanskrit: na te nāthaṃ yamy atrāham asmi na te nūnaṃ tanvā saṃ papṛcyām | asaṃyad etan manaso hṛdo me bhrātā svasuḥ śayane yac chayīya ||
english: Yamī, I am here as your protector, yet I will certainly not mingle my body with yours. This would be uncontrolled in my mind and heart—that a brother should lie in his sister's bed.

sanskrit: bato batāsi yama naiva te mano hṛdayaṃ cāvidāma | anyā kila tvāṃ kakṣeva yuktaṃ pari ṣvajāte libujeva vṛkṣam ||
english: Alas, O Yama, we know not your mind and heart at all. Surely another woman embraces you as the armpit clings to the body, as a creeping vine clasps a tree.

sanskrit: tasya vā tvaṃ mana iccha sa vā tava- -adhā kṛṇusva saṃvidaṃ subhadrām ||
english: Desire the mind of that one, or let him desire yours—then make a blessed union with him.

sanskrit: trīṇi chandāṃsi kavayo vi cetire pururūpaṃ darśataṃ viśvacakṣaṇam | vātā āpa oṣadhayas tāny ekasmin bhuvana ārpitāni ||
english: The sages have discerned three meters—manifold in form, visible, all-seeing. Winds, waters, and plants: all these are fixed within a single world.

sanskrit: vṛṣā vṛṣṇe duduhe dohasā divaḥ payāṃsi yahvo aditer adābhyaḥ | viśvaṃ sa veda varuṇo yathā dhiyā sa yajñiyo yajati yajñiyām̐ ṛtūn ||
english: The bull has milked for the bull the milkings of the sky—the youthful, inviolable offspring of Aditi. He knows all things as Varuṇa knows by his thought; being worthy of sacrifice, he sacrifices at the seasons worthy of sacrifice.

sanskrit: rapad gandharvīr apyā ca yoṣaṇā nadasya nāde pari pātu no manaḥ | iṣṭasya madhye aditir nu pātu no bhrātā no jyeṣṭhaḥ prathamo vi vocati ||
english: May the Gandharvas and the water maidens guard our mind in the sound of the stream. In the midst of the sacrifice, may Aditi now protect us—our eldest brother, the first one, speaks forth for us.

sanskrit: so cin nu bhadrā kṣumati yaśasvaty uṣā uvāsa manave svarvatī | yad īm uśantam uśatām anu kratum agniṃ hotāraṃ vidathāya jījanan ||
english: That auspicious, flaxen-clothed, glorious Dawn, rich in light, has shone for Manu—she who gave birth to Agni the hotar, the one eager among the eager, following their will, for the assembly.

sanskrit: adha tyaṃ drapsaṃ vibhavaṃ vicakṣaṇaṃ dvir ābharad viṣitaḥ śyeno adhvare | yadi viśo vṛṇate dasmam āryā agniṃ hotāram adha dhīr ajāyata ||
english: Then the eagle, unbound, carried that drop—abundant, all-seeing—twice to the sacrifice. When the noble Ārya clans choose the wondrous one as their hotar, Agni, then wisdom is born.

sanskrit: sadāsi raṇvo yavaseva puṣyate hotrābhir agne manuṣaḥ svadhvaraḥ | viprasya vā yac chaśamāna ukthyaṃ vājaṃ śasyavām̐ upayāhi bhūribhiḥ ||
english: You are ever joyful, nourished like grain, O Agni—man's rightful sacrifice made full through the priestly calls. Or come to us with your many strengths toward the laudable prize that the sage, striving, recites.

sanskrit: ud īraya pitarā jāra ābhiśam iyakṣati haryato hṛtta iṣyati | vivakti vahniḥ svapasyate makhas taviṣyate asuro vepate matīn ||
english: The lover rouses the two parents up face to face; the beloved one wishes to sacrifice, is gladdened, impelled. The carrier speaks aloud, the vigorous one performs good service, the lord of might grows powerful, the inspired one stirs the prayers.

sanskrit: yas te agne sumatiṃ martyo akṣata sahasaḥ sūno 'ti sa pra śṛṇve | iṣaṃ dadhāno vahamāno aśvair ā sa dyumām̐ amavān bhūṣati dyūn ||
english: The mortal who has obtained your good favor, O Agni, son of strength—he is celebrated far and wide. Holding refreshment, carried by horses, he, resplendent and mighty, adorns the days.

sanskrit: śrudhī no agne sadane sadhasthe yukṣyu ratham amṛtasya dravitnum | ā no vaha rodasī vedaputre mākir devānām apa bhūr iha syāḥ ||
english: Hear us, O Agni, in the dwelling, in the assembly place—yoke the chariot to race toward immortality. Bring the two worlds to us, O son of the Veda; may you not be absent here from the gods.

sanskrit: yad agna eṣā samitir bhavāti devī deveṣu yajatā yajatra | ratnā ca yad vi bhajāsi svadhāvo bhāgaṃ no atra vasumantaṃ vītāt ||
english: When this divine assembly takes place among the gods, O worthy of sacrifice among the adorable, O Agni, and when you distribute the jewels according to your nature—let a portion rich in wealth reach us here.

sanskrit: praty agnir uṣasām agram akhyat praty ahāni prathamo jātavedāḥ | prati sūryasya purutrā ca raśmīn prati dyāvāpṛthivī ā tatāna ||
english: Agni gazed forth at the forefront of the dawns, first of all Jātavedas he gazed at the days. He stretched out against the rays of the sun in many places; he stretched out against heaven and earth.

sanskrit: anv agnir uṣasām agram akhyad anv ahāni prathamo jātavedāḥ | anu sūryasya purutrā ca raśmīn anu dyāvāpṛthivī ā tatāna ||
english: Agni gazed along after the forefront of the dawns; first of all Jātavedas he gazed along after the days. He stretched out along after the rays of the sun in many places; he stretched out along after heaven and earth.

sanskrit: dyāvā ha kṣāmā prathame ṛtena- -abhisrāve bhavataḥ pratyavācāḥ | devo yan martān yatathāya kṛṇvan sīdad dhotā pratyaṅ svam asūn ||
english: Heaven and earth, the primeval ones, by truth come to be heard in response, speaking back. When the god, making mortals capable of their tasks, the hotar seated facing inward, his own life-breaths.

sanskrit: devo devān paribhūr ṛtena vahā no havyaṃ prathamaś cikitvān | dhūmaketuḥ samidhā bhāṛjīko mandro hotā nityo vācā yajīyān ||
english: The god who encompasses the gods by truth—first and knowing, carry our oblation. With smoke as his banner, blazing with kindling, the joyful eternal hotar, most worthy of worship with voice.

sanskrit: arcāmi vāṃ vardhāyāpo ghṛtasnū dyāvābhūmi śṛṇutaṃ rodasī me | ahā yad devā asunītim āyan madhvā no atra pitarā śaśītām ||
english: I hymn you two for increase, O waters dripping ghee—O Heaven and Earth, hear me, O the two worlds. When the gods approached the guiding of life-breaths on those days, may the two parents sharpen us here with sweetness.

sanskrit: svāvṛg devasyāmṛtaṃ yadī gor ato jātāso dhārayanta urvī | viśve devā anu tat te yajur gur duhe yad enī divyaṃ ghṛtaṃ vāḥ ||
english: The self-moving immortality of the god from the cow—those born from it hold wide space. All the All-Gods followed that Yajus of yours; when the tawny one milked the divine ghee for you.

sanskrit: kiṃ svin no rājā jagṛhe kad asya- -ati vrataṃ cakṛmā ko vi veda | mitraś cid dhi ṣmā juhurāṇo devān śloko na yātān api vājo asti ||
english: What has the king seized from us? What transgression against his law have we committed? Who indeed knows? For even Mitra, calling the gods deceitfully, there is still vigor, like a shout toward those who have come.

sanskrit: durmantv atrāmṛtasya nāma salakṣmā yad viṣurūpā bhavāti | yamasya yo manavate sumantv agne tam ṛṣva pāhy aprayucchan ||
english: May those think ill here of the name of immortality when one of the same mark becomes of differing form. But him who thinks well of Yama's ways, O Agni—protect that one, O great one, without faltering.

sanskrit: yasmin devā vidathe mādayante vivasvataḥ sadane dhārayante | sūrye jyotir adadhur māsy aktūn pari tad dyotanaṃ carato ajasrā ||
english: In whose assembly the gods rejoice, in whose dwelling the offspring of Vivasvat sustain themselves—they have placed light in the sun, nights in the moon; that luminance moves about them without ceasing.

sanskrit: yasmin devā manmani saṃcaranty apācye tye na vayam asya vidma | mitro no atrāditir anāgān savitā devo varuṇāya vocat ||
english: In whose thought the gods move together—those southward ones, which we do not know. May Mitra here, Aditi sinless, may the god Savitṛ speak to Varuṇa for us.

sanskrit: sakhāya ā śiṣāmahe brahmendrāya vajriṇe | stuṣa ū ṣu nṛtamāya dhṛṣṇave ||
english: As companions we desire sacred prayer for Indra the wielder of the vajra. I would praise him, the most manly, the bold one.

sanskrit: śavasā hy asi śruto vṛtrahatyena vṛtrahā | maghair maghono ati śūra dāsasi ||
english: For by your strength you are renowned, O slayer of Vṛtra, by the slaying of Vṛtra. With your gifts you surpass the generous, O hero.

sanskrit: stego na kṣām aty eṣi pṛthivīṃ mahī nu vātā ihā vāntu bhūmau | mitro no atra varuṇo ajyamāno 'gnir vane na vy asṛṣṭa śokam ||
english: Like a roof you pass over the earth, the great one—let the winds now blow here on the ground. May Mitra here and Varuṇa, ungrasped, may Agni release his flame as in the forest for us.

sanskrit: stuhi śrutaṃ gartasadaṃ janānāṃ rājānaṃ bhīmam upahatnum ugram | mṛḍā jaritre rudra stavāno anyaṃ te asman ni vapantu senyam ||
english: Praise the renowned one who sits in the chariot, the king of peoples, the fearsome, the smiting, the fierce. Be gracious to the singer, O Rudra, when praised—may they lay upon another the destructive weapon meant for us.
